text:
harper: FYI customer AcmeAI reporting a sudden spike of 502/504s on hosted inference starting ~08:12 UTC. They say errors correlate with auth token rotation and large embed batches. trace id example: trace-abc123.
aj: On it — do we have a sample request or curl to reproduce?
harper: They sent this curl + payload snippet.
harper: `curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token>\" -H \"X-Tenant: acme\" -d @payload.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings`
sam: Checking metrics now. @sre-oncall-bot can you dump 5xx counts for edge-gateway for tenant=acme in the last 15m?
sre-oncall-bot: edge.gateway.502s: 472 in last 15m for tenant:acme, spike peak at 08:13 UTC. h2 upstream resets elevated.
lucy: That pattern smells like keepalive/connpool exhaustion around token swap. Was there a key/token rotation at ~08:10?
devon: Customer confirms they rotated tokens at 08:11 and kicked off parallel embed batches. Auth backend saw a flood of validation calls and throttled. Could be upstream slow -> resets.
aj: Can someone pull envoy/midfront logs for trace-abc123? I suspect \"upstream connect error or disconnect\" entries.
harper: Excerpt from envoy logs: ```envoy error: cluster \"midfront\" failed to respond: upstream connection reset by peer, code: 14```
sam: Immediate hypothesis: midfront pod(s) restarted or hit OOM during large batches, dropping active upstream connections -> 502 cascade.
lucy: If midfront restarted during token swap, all pooled connections die and client retries cause spikes. We should check pod restarts and OOM events.
aj: I grabbed traces: trace-abc123 and trace-abc124. Both show h2 GOAWAY around 08:12:52 and multiple upstream reset frames.
sre-oncall-bot: event: pod midfront-7f8b restarted at 08:12:50 due to OOMKilled (kubelet).
devon: OOMKilled explains midfront restart -> dropped connections -> envoy returned 502/504 to clients. Repro likely when token refresh causes burst of short-lived new connections plus heavy embedding memory.
harper: Proposed immediate mitigations: 1) bump auth cache TTL for tenant acme to avoid auth backend spike during their rotations, 2) scale midfront up by +2 replicas, 3) ask customer to avoid rotating tokens during heavy parallel batches while we patch.
sam: I can flip a tenant-scoped authCacheTTL to 60s and scale midfront. Lucy, can you confirm the safe kubectl patch?
lucy: Command I'm about to run: ```bash
kubectl patch deploy edge-config -n prod --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/authCacheTTL","value":"60s"}]'
``` Need approver from oncall for tenant change.
aj: Also do a short-term keepalive/conn limit tweak on midfront: lower idle keepalive to reduce stuck sockets and raise per-host connection limit to handle bursts. That reduces connection churn on restart.
harper: Customer repro steps to share: 1) start 20 parallel embed requests against hosted API, 2) rotate bearer token during the burst, 3) observe intermittent 502/504s. Quick repro script: ```bash
for i in {1..20}; do
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Tenant: acme" -d @payload.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings &
done
wait
# rotate token now (customer side)
```
aj: Confirmed: traces show midfront restart + h2 GOAWAYs.
sre-oncall-bot: alert cleared? 5xx rate returned to baseline after scale-bump at 08:15 and TTL bump at 08:14.
sam: Root cause summary: midfront OOM during burst concurrent embeddings while customer rotated tokens -> pod restart -> upstream connection resets -> edge returned 502/504.
lucy: Longer-term fixes: enforce circuit-breaker on auth validation path, add graceful connection draining for midfront restarts, increase midfront memory headroom for batching, and tune auth cache behavior during rotation.
harper: Immediate actions taken: bumped authCacheTTL to 60s for tenant acme and scaled midfront +2 replicas. 5xx dropped to normal within ~2 minutes. Customer notified.
aj: Can you paste a short customer-facing summary we'll send to AcmeAI? Keep it simple and actionable.
harper: Draft customer message: \"We observed transient 502/504 errors during your token rotation window caused by a midfront pod OOM and restart. We applied a temporary mitigation (auth cache TTL increase + scaled midfront). To avoid recurrence, please stagger token rotations away from large concurrent batch jobs; we'll follow up with a permanent memory/config change and improved draining. Apologies for the disruption.\"
devon: :thumbsup: I'll open a PR to increase midfront memory limits and add preStop drain hook.
sam: Links for internal follow-up: Grafana panel (502s): https://grafana.redwood/dashboard/edge?panel=502s&tenant=acme and traces: https://traces.redwood/trace/trace-abc123
harper: I'll close this thread after we confirm PR merged and customer ack. Thanks all.
